[
  {"sentence": 1, "status": "present", "evidence": "Prologue: on the sinking Lusitania a frightened man gives an American girl 'vitally important papers' in an oilskin packet 'because of \"women and children first\"'; Carter later names him Danvers and her Jane Finn.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 2, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Tommy, old thing!' 'Tuppence, old bean!' ... Prudence Cowley, 'fifth daughter of Archdeacon Cowley'; 'Good old hospital--demobbed'; Tommy 'finally got demobbed'.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 3, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Tommy, you're stony!' ... 'Trading under the name of the Young Adventurers, Ltd.?' 'Two young adventurers for hire.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 4, "status": "present", "evidence": "Whittington: 'I happened to overhear part of your conversation' ... offers £100 to 're-enter one of those charming pensionnats de jeunes filles' in Paris.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 5, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Jane Finn,' she said hastily ... Whittington purple with rage and 'incredulous dismay'; 'Here's fifty to go on with'; next day the office is closed and the company 'left rather suddenly'.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 6, "status": "present", "evidence": "'The advertisement has appeared, and--there are only two answers!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 7, "status": "present", "evidence": "First letter signed 'A. CARTER.'", "note": "Sentence fragment, read together with sentence 8."},
  {"sentence": 8, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Yes, sir, I recognized you at once. Saw you in France when I was with the Intelligence.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 9, "status": "present", "evidence": "'the draft of a secret agreement' ... 'it undoubtedly implicates a number of our statesmen' ... 'Bolshevist gold is pouring into this country to procure a Revolution'; Carter also refers to 'the strike menace'.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 10, "status": "present", "evidence": "'He is always spoken of by the unassuming title of \"Mr. Brown.\"'", "note": "Sentence fragment, read together with sentence 11."},
  {"sentence": 11, "status": "present", "evidence": "'a certain man, whose real name is unknown to us'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 12, "status": "present", "evidence": "'How would you like to work for me? ... Find Jane Finn.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 13, "status": "present", "evidence": "Second letter signed 'JULIUS P. HERSHEIMMER.'", "note": "Sentence fragment, read together with sentence 14."},
  {"sentence": 14, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Jane Finn. My father and her mother were brother and sister' ... 'Inspector Brown' took 'the only copy in existence' of her photograph ... afterwards 'All barriers went down with a crash.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 15, "status": "present", "evidence": "Tuppence reasons that Danvers was shadowed, probably by a woman who may have been 'Rita'; they work through the Lusitania survivor list.", "note": "Sentence fragment, read together with sentence 16."},
  {"sentence": 16, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Mrs. Vandemeyer, 20 South Audley Mansions' ... 'Marguerite ... She's mostly called that [Rita], sir.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 17, "status": "present", "evidence": "Tommy follows Boris to a Soho house, knocks with the signal knock and says 'Mr. Brown?'; the doorkeeper replies 'Upstairs.'", "note": "Sentence fragment, read together with sentence 18."},
  {"sentence": 18, "status": "present", "evidence": "Tommy overhears the meeting; Number One is later identified as Kramenin; 'And--the date, my friend?' 'The 29th.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 19, "status": "present", "evidence": "'A crashing blow descended on his head' ... he proposes 'My life and liberty against ... The papers that Danvers brought over' ... 'I believe that I can find them.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 20, "status": "present", "evidence": "The lift-boy Albert arranges the post for her: 'I'll fix the whole thing up in two ticks.'", "note": "Sentence fragment, read together with sentence 21."},
  {"sentence": 21, "status": "present", "evidence": "Mrs. Vandemeyer hires her as house-parlourmaid under the name 'Prudence Cooper'.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 22, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Sir James Peel Edgerton ... the famous K.C.'", "note": "Sentence fragment, read together with sentence 23."},
  {"sentence": 23, "status": "present", "evidence": "'And a change does no harm sometimes ... Just a hint'; later 'I've a good mind to stay, and see if we can't get on the track of that young chap.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 24, "status": "present", "evidence": "'a rim of cold steel touched her temple'", "note": "Sentence fragment, read together with sentences 25 and 26."},
  {"sentence": 25, "status": "present", "evidence": "Tuppence seizes the revolver ('Now who's on top?') and offers 'a hundred thousand' from 'an American millionaire'.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 26, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Who is Mr. Brown?' ... 'Yes, I know.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 27, "status": "present", "evidence": "Mrs. Vandemeyer faints at the sight of Sir James and Julius in the doorway; after the night-long vigil she is found dead in the morning ('odour of chloral', the bottle empty).", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 28, "status": "present", "evidence": "Dr. Hall had 'Janet Vandemeyer' at his Bournemouth home, 'suffering from a complete loss of memory'; she 'is no longer under my care'.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 29, "status": "present", "evidence": "Julius proposes ('What about me?'); Tuppence afterwards cries 'I do love you so' over Tommy's photo and writes to Julius 'Let's leave it till then.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 30, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Telegram for you, miss.' ... 'Come at once, Moat House, Ebury, Yorkshire, great developments--TOMMY.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 31, "status": "present", "evidence": "Annette slips him a penknife and helps him escape, crying 'To Marguerite!'; at the Ritz 'Miss Cowley had gone out a quarter of an hour ago.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 32, "status": "present", "evidence": "'A week! We're no nearer to finding Tuppence'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 33, "status": "present", "evidence": "Telegram 'Jane Finn found ... PEEL EDGERTON'; following the girl's directions they reach a cliff path at Holyhead and find the packet: 'WITH THE COMPLIMENTS OF MR. BROWN.'", "note": "Sentence spans the break into sentence 34."},
  {"sentence": 34, "status": "present", "evidence": "Tuppence's green toque and coat 'Washed up on the Yorkshire coast'; Tommy to Julius: 'but I loved her.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 35, "status": "present", "evidence": "'What on earth was a photograph of the French girl Annette doing in Julius Hersheimmer's writing-table?'; Tommy's letter to Carter: 'that girl at Manchester was just a plant.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 36, "status": "present", "evidence": "'I kept my mind open between the two of them.'", "note": "Sentence fragment, read together with sentence 37."},
  {"sentence": 37, "status": "present", "evidence": "Tommy leaves Julius a note claiming he is off to the Argentine and leaves Sir James's letter where Julius will see it; the original telegram leads to 'Astley Priors, Gatehouse, Kent.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 38, "status": "present", "evidence": "'She'd never spell her name \"Twopence\" ... Julius had seen it ... but Sir James hadn't!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 39, "status": "present", "evidence": "Julius holds Kramenin at gunpoint ('Hands up--or I shoot!') and has him bring both girls out of Astley Priors; Jane: 'Been fooling them all the time' ... 'Five long years!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 40, "status": "present", "evidence": "'That's why I sent the girls off to Sir James ... I was sure they'd fetch up at the house in Soho'; the papers are behind the picture 'Marguerite with her casket of jewels'.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 41, "status": "present", "evidence": "Jane rips the backing off the picture and extracts the treaty; Sir James: 'I am Mr. Brown.'", "note": "Sentence fragment, read together with sentence 42."},
  {"sentence": 42, "status": "present", "evidence": "As he raises the automatic he is 'seized from behind in a grip of iron' by Julius and Tommy, who had hidden 'behind the curtain in the recess'.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 43, "status": "present", "evidence": "'the hand which bore the big signet ring, was raised to his lips' ... 'an odour of bitter almonds filled the air.'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 44, "status": "present", "evidence": "'Deprived of their chief, the organization fell to pieces' ... the treaty 'reduced to ashes' ... 'It was to be Peace, not War!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 45, "status": "present", "evidence": "At the Savoy supper Carter reads from 'a small shabby brown book'; Sir William: 'Shall we let bygones be bygones ... You're my heir'; Carter toasts Jane as 'one of the bravest of America's daughters!'", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 46, "status": "present", "evidence": "Julius: 'Jane--I want you to marry me!' Jane: 'I love you now, Julius'; in the taxi Tommy says 'You won't be able to get out of marrying me' and Tuppence speaks of 'Ours'.", "note": ""},
  {"sentence": 47, "status": "present", "evidence": "'But do you know what I think it is?' 'What?' 'A sport!' 'And a damned good sport too.'", "note": "The theme of pluck and common sense defeating villainy runs through the whole abridgment."}
]
